name: Dart
tools: dart CLI (analyze, format, fix, test, compile)
Visual Studio Code with the Dart extension
IntelliJ IDEA with the Dart plugin

beginner.summary: For developers who already program in another language such as Python, Java, JavaScript or C# and are new to Dart. Covers the SDK and dart CLI, types and sound null safety, control flow, functions, collections, classes, mixins, enums, generics, records and patterns, sealed classes, exceptions, Futures and async, dart:io files, pub packages, testing, linting, and a command-line capstone. Flutter is not required.
prerequisites: Writes working programs in at least one other language
Uses a terminal confidently: changing directories, running commands and reading output
Has a Windows, macOS or Linux machine with rights to install the Dart SDK and an editor such as Visual Studio Code
outcomes: Install the Dart SDK and build, run, analyse, format, test and compile programs with the dart CLI
Write null-safe, strongly typed Dart using classes, mixins, generics, records, patterns and sealed types
Handle errors and asynchronous work with exceptions, Futures and async and await
Build, test and compile a command-line tool that uses pub packages and local files

intermediate.summary: For Dart developers who know the basics and need production habits. Covers flow analysis and promotion, class modifiers, extension types, lazy iterables, equality, the event loop, streams, async patterns, isolates, zones, JSON code generation, HTTP clients, package publishing, mocking and coverage, command-line tools with package:args, processes and signals, sharing pure-Dart code with Flutter, and a concurrent link-checker capstone.
prerequisites: Completed a beginner Dart course or has equivalent experience with classes, null safety, Futures and pub
Can write and run tests with package:test
Is comfortable with Git and a command-line workflow
outcomes: Use class modifiers, extension types and patterns to model data safely
Design concurrent programs with streams, futures, zones and isolates
Build, test and publish-ready packages and command-line tools with generated JSON code and HTTP clients
Measure test coverage and test asynchronous and time-dependent code deterministically

advanced.summary: For experienced Dart developers building performance-sensitive tools and servers. Covers the VM, garbage collection, profiling with DevTools, benchmarking, isolate worker pools, FFI, build hooks and native assets, Dart on the web with JavaScript and WebAssembly, compile targets and cross-compilation, server-side Dart with shelf, dart:io, WebSockets, databases, security, gRPC, Dart Frog and Serverpod, containers and Cloud Run, observability, workspaces, code generation, dependency governance, and a job-queue capstone.
prerequisites: Completed an intermediate Dart course or has shipped Dart packages or tools
Understands async, streams and isolates and can write tests
Has Docker installed and can read basic SQL and HTTP traces
outcomes: Profile, benchmark and tune Dart programs using DevTools and AOT builds
Integrate native code and JavaScript or WebAssembly targets with FFI and js_interop
Build secure, observable, containerised Dart servers with databases and gRPC
Govern dependencies and large Dart codebases with workspaces, code generation and CI checks
